lecture_summary: The lecture connects translational and rotational kinematics; distinguishes angular, tangential, and radial acceleration; applies constant-angular-acceleration equations to a disk stopping; interprets θ–ω–α graphs; and uses angular-vector signs and the right-hand rule to determine rotational directions.

videos.title: Velocity Time Graphs, Acceleration & Position Time Graphs - Physics
videos.reason: Reviews the graph-based reasoning that transfers directly from x–v–a plots to θ–ω–α plots, including slopes, areas, and determining whether motion is speeding up or slowing down.

videos.title: Rotational Motion Physics, Basic Introduction, Angular Velocity & Tangential Acceleration
videos.reason: Provides the central conceptual bridge from translation to rotation and covers angular displacement, angular velocity, angular acceleration, tangential acceleration, and inward centripetal acceleration.

videos.title: Rotational Kinematics Physics Problems, Basic Introduction, Equations & Formulas
videos.reason: Supplies the closest representative problem practice for selecting and applying constant-angular-acceleration equations to find angular acceleration, displacement, stopping time, and related quantities.

coverage_gaps: No strong rotation-specific playlist match covers angular velocity and angular acceleration as axial vectors, viewpoint dependence, or the right-hand rule for v⃗ = ω⃗ × r⃗. The playlist’s right-hand-rule videos are electromagnetism-specific.
The graph video treats translational rather than rotational plots, so the exact shapes and interpretation of α(t), ω(t), and θ(t) for a slowing disk are covered only by analogy.
The playlist metadata does not confirm focused treatment of s = rθ, radians-to-revolutions conversion, or the lecture’s exact 12 rad/s disk-stopping example.
